title: Renal cell carcinoma
subtitle: Management by histology (clear cell vs non-clear cell) and IMDC risk. Localized disease is surgical ± adjuvant pembrolizumab; metastatic clear cell gets an IO backbone (IO/TKI or ipi/nivo) with no predictive biomarker; after IO progression, switch mechanism; IO rechallenge not beneficial (CONTACT-03)
source: Compiled from the Stanford Oncology Handbook 2025, GU: Renal Cell Carcinoma (Ruiz SM, Fan AC) · NCCN · primary trial reports and FDA actions verified against PubMed, September 2026.

blocks.heading: Workup
items: Most are found incidentally on imaging; the classic triad (flank pain, hematuria, mass) is seen in only ~10%
Paraneoplastic: erythrocytosis (EPO), hypercalcemia (PTHrP), hypertension (renin), Stauffer syndrome (cholestasis without liver mets — resolves after nephrectomy)

CT abdomen/pelvis with contrast (MRI if poor renal function, IVC thrombus, or to call fat in an angiomyolipoma) + chest CT. Brain MRI and bone scan when symptomatic or before systemic therapy in high-risk disease

Biopsy is not required before nephrectomy for a solid enhancing mass — get it for small masses when it would change AS vs treatment, suspected lymphoma/metastasis/infection, or before systemic therapy without surgery
Labs that feed IMDC: CBC with differential, calcium, plus LDH, creatinine, LFTs
Genetics referral (NCCN): RCC at age ≤46, bilateral or multifocal tumors, ≥1 first/second-degree relative with RCC, or a somatic hit with germline implications

blocks.heading: Staging (AJCC 8th)
rows: Confined to kidney, ≤7 cm — T1a ≤4 cm, T1b >4–7 cm
Confined to kidney, >7 cm — T2a ≤10 cm, T2b >10 cm
Major veins or perinephric fat, not beyond Gerota's — a renal vein / sinus or perirenal fat · b IVC below diaphragm · c IVC above diaphragm or caval wall
Beyond Gerota's fascia, incl. contiguous ipsilateral adrenal
I T1N0 · II T2N0 · III T1–2N1 or T3 any N · IV T4 or M1
blocks.footnote: Grade (WHO/ISUP) is nucleolar: G1–G3 by nucleolar prominence at 400×/100×; G4 = marked pleomorphism, giant cells, rhabdoid or sarcomatoid.

blocks.heading: IMDC risk
blocks.footnote: Favorable = 0 · Intermediate = 1–2 · Poor = ≥3. Two clinical + four labs. Prognostic, and it is how the 1L trials were stratified — but it does not predict IO vs TKI benefit except that ipi/nivo underperforms in favorable risk.

blocks.heading: After nephrectomy
items: Surveillance (NCCN, risk-adapted): history, labs and chest/abdominal imaging every 3–6 months for ~3 years after stage II–III, then annually to year 5 and beyond — RCC recurs late, sometimes a decade or more after surgery
Unusual metastatic sites are classic: pancreas, thyroid, adrenal, skin, and hypervascular brain lesions that bleed

boxes: T1a: partial nephrectomy, ablation <3 cm, or AS
T1b–T3: partial if feasible, else radical
renal vein / IVC thrombus: still resectable
pT2 G4/sarcomatoid, ≥pT3, N+, or M1 NED

chains.header: Metastatic clear cell — first line by IMDC
boxes: sarcomatoid: IO combination, not TKI alone
no triplet — COSMIC-313 had no OS gain
selected only — usually deferred after response
switch to a VEGF TKI: cabozantinib, axitinib,
belz + lenvatinib: FDA decision due 4 Oct 2026

blocks.heading: Histology
rows: VHL loss (3p) → HIF-2α accumulation → VEGF. Why VEGF TKIs, IO and belzutifan work; chemo-resistant
MET-driven subset (chr 7 gain, MET alterations). Cabozantinib best randomized data
Usually indolent; IO barely works. BHD (FLCN) association
Aggressive, often metastatic at diagnosis — treat like urothelial: gemcitabine + platinum
Young patients with sickle cell trait; SMARCB1 (INI1) loss. Platinum-based chemo; dismal prognosis
TFE3/TFEB (MiT family); children and young adults
Not a subtype but dedifferentiation — poor prognosis, yet the best responders to IO

blocks.heading: Localized disease & surgery
items: Small renal mass (≤4 cm): active surveillance is legitimate, especially in the elderly or comorbid — many are benign or indolent. Serial imaging; intervene for growth (~>5 mm/yr) or size >3–4 cm. Ablation (cryo/RFA) for <3 cm
Partial nephrectomy preferred for T1a (and T1b when feasible) to protect renal function.
IVC tumor thrombus is not a contraindication to resection. Lymphadenectomy has no proven OS benefit; no role for adjuvant RT

Cytoreductive nephrectomy is no longer routine: CARMENA — sunitinib alone non-inferior (OS 18.4 vs 13.9 mo); SURTIME — deferred CN after 3 cycles of sunitinib gave longer OS (exploratory). Keep it for good PS, low-volume disease, symptomatic primary, or a responder with residual primary
Metastasectomy / SBRT for oligometastatic disease, especially with a long disease-free interval

blocks.heading: Pearls
items: No chemotherapy for clear cell — the only chemo-sensitive RCCs are collecting duct and medullary
Renal mass + sickle cell trait in a young Black patient = medullary carcinoma until proven otherwise
Belzutifan is the VHL drug (hereditary) and a later-line drug in sporadic ccRCC — same target, HIF-2α
Cabozantinib appears at every step: 1L (with nivo or alone), 2L after IO (METEOR, CONTACT-03 control arm), and papillary (PAPMET)

pages.subtitle: Page 2 — adjuvant, first line, later lines, non-clear cell and hereditary RCC

blocks.heading: Adjuvant therapy
rows: Pembrolizumab ×1 yr vs placebo — DFS HR 0.68; OS HR 0.62 (48-mo OS 91.2% vs 86.0%). The first adjuvant therapy in RCC with an OS benefit
Pembro + belzutifan vs pembro — DFS HR 0.72, 24-mo DFS 80.7% vs 73.7%. OS immature (HR 0.78, NS); grade ≥3 AEs 52% vs 30%. FDA approved 12 Jun 2026
blocks.footnote: Clear cell only. Every other adjuvant IO trial (nivo ± ipi, atezolizumab, perioperative nivo) was negative, and no adjuvant TKI improved survival (sunitinib, S-TRAC, gained DFS only and is rarely used) — pembrolizumab-based therapy is the adjuvant option.

blocks.heading: First-line clear cell — all vs sunitinib unless stated
rows: Int/poor: OS HR 0.69 at 8 yr, CR 11.8% vs 2.6%, median DOR 82.8 mo — the most durable tail. Favorable: OS HR 0.82 (NS), ORR 30% vs 52%. PFS co-primary missed its α
Final (43 mo): OS HR 0.73, PFS HR 0.68, ORR 60% vs 40%. All risk groups
Final (5.6 yr): OS 46.5 vs 35.5 mo, HR 0.79; PFS 16.4 vs 8.3 mo; ORR 55.7% vs 27.4%, CR 13.9%. Best QoL data
PFS 23.9 vs 9.2 mo (HR 0.47), ORR 71.3% — highest response rate. Final OS HR 0.79, medians equal (53.7 vs 54.3 mo)
vs ipi/nivo, int/poor — PFS 16.6 vs 11.2 mo (HR 0.82) but OS HR 1.02, grade 3–4 AEs 79% vs 56%. Triplet rejected
Int/poor, randomized phase 2 — PFS 8.2 vs 5.6 mo. The IO-ineligible option
blocks.footnote: No head-to-head trial between IO combinations and no predictive biomarker (PD-L1 does not select). Pick by risk group, comorbidity, and whether you want response (IO/TKI) or a durable treatment-free tail (ipi/nivo).

blocks.heading: First-line regimen choice
items: Symptomatic, bulky, or need a response now → IO/TKI; lenvatinib + pembro has the highest ORR and longest PFS
Int/poor risk, want a chance at a durable treatment-free remission → ipi/nivo; also avoids chronic TKI toxicity. Expect front-loaded irAEs
Favorable risk → IO/TKI (ipi/nivo lost on ORR and PFS); indolent low-volume disease can be watched
Autoimmune disease, transplant, or IO-ineligible → cabozantinib (int/poor) or sunitinib/pazopanib
Relapse after adjuvant pembrolizumab: no randomized data — most use a VEGF TKI-based regimen, especially if relapse occurs on or soon after IO

blocks.heading: Second line and beyond
rows: Belzutifan + lenvatinib vs cabozantinib after anti-PD-(L)1 — PFS 14.8 vs 10.7 mo (HR 0.70), ORR ~53% vs ~40%; interim OS HR 0.85, not significant (final pending). FDA action date 4 Oct 2026
Belzutifan vs everolimus after IO + TKI — ORR 21.9% vs 3.5%, 18-mo PFS 24% vs 8%, but median PFS 5.6 mo in both and OS HR 0.88, NS. FDA 14 Dec 2023
Cabozantinib vs everolimus after VEGF TKI — OS 21.4 vs 16.5 mo (HR 0.66), PFS HR 0.51
Nivolumab vs everolimus after VEGF TKI — OS 25.0 vs 19.6 mo (HR 0.73); the IO-naive 2L option
Lenvatinib + everolimus vs everolimus, randomized phase 2 — PFS 14.6 vs 5.5 mo (HR 0.40)
Tivozanib vs sorafenib after ≥2 lines — PFS 5.6 vs 3.9 mo; no OS benefit
Adding atezolizumab or nivolumab to a TKI after IO — no benefit
blocks.footnote: Do not rechallenge IO. After IO, the next drug is a VEGF TKI; belzutifan comes after IO + TKI.

blocks.heading: Non-clear cell — mostly single-arm data
rows: Cabozantinib vs sunitinib, randomized phase 2 — PFS 9.0 vs 5.6 mo (HR 0.60), ORR 23% vs 4%; OS NS. Savolitinib and crizotinib arms closed for futility
Lenvatinib + pembro, single-arm — ORR 49% (51% at 2 yr), sarcomatoid 47%
Cabo + nivo — ORR 47.5% papillary/unclassified; 0 of 7 chromophobe responded
IO largely inactive; VEGF TKI ± mTOR (e.g., lenvatinib + everolimus). Trial preferred
Gemcitabine + cisplatin/carboplatin; TKIs and IO rarely help. Check sickle status in a young patient with a renal mass
Use an IO combination whatever the parent histology — the highest CR rates in 1L subgroups

blocks.heading: Hereditary syndromes (all autosomal dominant)
rows: Clear cell, multifocal/bilateral; CNS/retinal hemangioblastomas, pheochromocytoma, pNET, pancreatic cysts. Belzutifan (LITESPARK-004: RCC ORR 49%; FDA Aug 2021) spares repeated surgery; resect when the largest tumor reaches ~3 cm
FH-deficient RCC — solitary, aggressive, metastasizes early: excise promptly, no surveillance. Cutaneous + uterine leiomyomas. Advanced: erlotinib + bevacizumab (ORR 72%, mPFS 21.1 mo)
Chromophobe / hybrid oncocytic, bilateral; fibrofolliculomas, lung cysts → pneumothorax
Aggressive clear cell; uveal and cutaneous melanoma, mesothelioma

pages.subtitle: Page 3 — regimen dosing, toxicity and monitoring, key trials

blocks.heading: Regimen dosing
rows: 200 mg IV q3wk ×17 or 400 mg q6wk (~1 yr)
Belzutifan 120 mg PO daily ×up to 54 wk with pembrolizumab 200 q3wk / 400 q6wk ×12 mo
Axitinib 5 mg PO BID (titrate to 7 then 10 mg BID if BP controlled) + pembrolizumab 200 mg q3wk / 400 q6wk, IO up to 2 yr
Nivolumab 3 mg/kg + ipilimumab 1 mg/kg IV q3wk ×4 → nivolumab 240 mg q2wk or 480 mg q4wk
Cabozantinib 40 mg PO daily (not 60) + nivolumab 240 q2wk / 480 q4wk, nivo max 2 yr
Lenvatinib 20 mg PO daily + pembrolizumab 200 q3wk / 400 q6wk, IO up to 2 yr
60 mg PO daily on an empty stomach; hold ≥3 wk before surgery
120 mg PO daily — after IO + VEGF TKI, and for VHL tumors
1.34 mg PO daily, 21 days on / 7 off — after ≥2 prior systemic lines
Lenvatinib 18 mg + everolimus 5 mg PO daily
5 mg BID → 7 → 10 mg BID if BP ≤150/90 and tolerated
50 mg PO daily, 4 wk on / 2 wk off (or 2 on / 1 off for tolerance)
Erlotinib 150 mg PO daily + bevacizumab 10 mg/kg IV q2wk — HLRCC / papillary
blocks.footnote: Pembrolizumab in RCC is 200 mg q3wk or 400 mg q6wk — not 300/600. Historical: high-dose IL-2 (ORR ~14%, rare durable CRs), temsirolimus (poor-risk, ARCC).

blocks.heading: Toxicity & monitoring
items: Hypertension is the signature VEGF-TKI toxicity — control BP before starting, home BP log, add agents early rather than stopping the TKI. Urine protein with lenvatinib and bevacizumab

Transaminitis on axitinib + pembrolizumab (or cabo/lenva + IO): hold both drugs. TKI hepatitis resolves within days (short half-lives); if ALT is not falling after ~1 week, or grade ≥3, treat as immune hepatitis with prednisone 1–2 mg/kg. Restart the TKI first at reduced dose; rechallenge IO only if it wasn't the culprit
Pazopanib carries a boxed warning for hepatotoxicity — LFTs before starting and every ~2 weeks through month 4; also QT prolongation
Hypothyroidism from both TKIs (sunitinib, axitinib, lenvatinib) and IO — TSH every 4–6 wk on treatment

Belzutifan: on-target anemia (HIF-2α drives EPO — decreased Hgb is the most common adverse reaction) and hypoxia: check Hgb and pulse oximetry at baseline and periodically; transfuse, hold or dose-reduce. Boxed warning: embryo-fetal toxicity, and it can make hormonal contraception ineffective
Ipi/nivo: front-loaded irAEs — colitis, hepatitis, hypophysitis, adrenal insufficiency. Check cortisol with fatigue or hyponatremia
Cabozantinib: diarrhea, hand-foot, stomatitis, wound-healing and bleeding — dose reductions to 40/20 mg are routine
Sunitinib: hand-foot, mucositis, cytopenias, cardiomyopathy. mTOR inhibitors: pneumonitis, hyperglycemia, hyperlipidemia
Bone metastases (lytic, ~1/3): zoledronic acid (renally dosed) or denosumab; brain metastases — SRS before or alongside systemic therapy

blocks.heading: Special situations
items: Brain metastases: treat locally first (SRS or resection); patients with treated, stable brain mets can receive standard systemic therapy
Dialysis / poor renal function: IO needs no renal adjustment; dose-adjust zoledronic acid, and denosumab carries a severe-hypocalcemia risk in advanced CKD
Pre-existing autoimmune disease or solid-organ transplant: avoid IO; TKI monotherapy
Surgery on a TKI: hold cabozantinib ≥3 wk before and resume only after wound healing; bevacizumab ≥28 days

blocks.heading: Key trials
rows: Adding belzutifan to adjuvant pembro — DFS HR 0.72, OS immature
Ipi/nivo, int/poor — 8-yr OS HR 0.69, durable CRs
Lenva + pembro — PFS 23.9 vs 9.2 mo, ORR 71%
Triplet cabo + ipi/nivo — PFS gain, no OS gain
Immediate cytoreductive nephrectomy not needed; defer and select
Belzutifan after IO + TKI (ORR 22%); + lenvatinib post-IO, PFS HR 0.70
Papillary: cabozantinib beats sunitinib on PFS
Belzutifan in VHL disease — RCC ORR 49%
IO/TKI vs sunitinib — final OS HR 0.73 / 0.79
Nivolumab after TKI — OS 25.0 vs 19.6 mo
HLRCC papillary RCC — ORR 72%, mPFS 21.1 mo

Toxicity & monitoring Hypertension is the signature VEGF-TKI toxicity — control BP before starting, home BP log, add agents early rather than stopping the TKI. Urine protein with lenvatinib and bevacizumab Transaminitis on axitinib + pembrolizumab (or cabo/lenva + IO): hold both drugs . TKI hepatitis resolves within days (short half-lives); if ALT is not falling after ~1 week, or grade ≥3, treat as immune hepatitis with prednisone 1–2 mg/kg. Restart the TKI first at reduced dose; rechallenge IO only if it wasn't the culprit Pazopanib carries a boxed warning for hepatotoxicity — LFTs before starting and every ~2 weeks through month 4; also QT prolongation Hypothyroidism from both TKIs (sunitinib, axitinib, lenvatinib) and IO — TSH every 4–6 wk on treatment Belzutifan: on-target anemia (HIF-2α drives EPO — decreased Hgb is the most common adverse reaction) and hypoxia : check Hgb and pulse oximetry at baseline and periodically; transfuse, hold or dose-reduce. Boxed warning: embryo-fetal toxicity , and it can make hormonal contraception ineffective Ipi/nivo: front-loaded irAEs — colitis, hepatitis, hypophysitis, adrenal insufficiency.
